sentence: This project studies how a fusion protein drives Ewing sarcoma development through a process known as phase separation.
This project develops computational methods that model enzymatic reactions and biomedical imaging probes quickly and accurately.
This project tries to find out whether fungi in the gut promote inflammation-associated pain.
This project studies how factors that modulate signaling control the neuron-glia switch in neural progenitor cells during development and after spinal cord injury.
This project provides resources for recombinant protein expression and supports the purification of oxygen-sensitive proteins.
This project works on biomedical imaging, which enables early disease detection and assessment of therapy.
This project tests whether an artificial intelligence breakthrough that predicts protein structures is accelerating health-relevant science.
This project develops a platform that uses long-read sequencing to study DNA sequence, chromatin structure, and protein binding in single molecules.
This project studies whether neural circuits in the cerebellum use rapid changes in synaptic strength to learn temporally precise motor behaviors.
This project uses nanobody technology to study how an executioner protein self-assembles into higher-order oligomers during programmed cell death.
This project studies the role of the retrotransposon Long Interspersed Nuclear Element-1 in type I interferon-mediated disease.
This project develops low-cost laboratory tools and teaching materials that help high school teachers bring hands-on synthetic and molecular biology activities into school classrooms.
This project studies how neuropeptides, the brain's signaling molecules, tune the same circuits differently in females and males.
This project studies how Rickettsia felis and the vector fleas interact to better understand an emerging flea-borne rickettsiosis.
This project studies how fibroblast growth factor 15 and 19 from the small intestine control drug metabolizing enzyme genes and liver drug metabolism.
This project develops a modeling platform that recreates the molecular differences of liver cancer through defined gene alterations.
This project validates wearable light sensors as a way to measure children's screen media use.
This project builds an automated way to assess robotic surgical skills using deep learning algorithms.
This project studies how cells in a tissue rearrange to split and how cells from different tissues interact to merge, using zebrafish.
This project studies how mitochondrial subpopulations inside and between cells change throughout life and influence aging.
